To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and applied a new method of muscle organelle proteomics to identify the reduction in the full length dystropin isoform and its dystrophin associated glycoprotein complex as well as the secondary proteomic changes in the mdX 4cv mouse, a model of human muscular dystrophy.
the organelle proteomics of dystrophin glycopeptide complexes and secondary changes in skeletal muscles can be achieved by the simple enrichment of the muscle microsomal fraction.

the proteomic analysis of the dystrophin associated membrane fraction in normal versus dystrophin deficient skeletal muscle identified the reduction of dystrophin and secondary changes in dystrophic muscle tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an organelle proteomics workflow for the comprehensive pathoproteomic evaluation of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex and associated proteins in the dystrophins deficient mdx 4 cv mouse model.
the development of a novel muscle pathoproteomic approach for the comprehensive characterization of the dystrophin associated protein complex.
the development of novel proteomic strategies for the simultaneous pathoproteomic profiling of the dystrophin complex and secondary changes of dystrophic skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dystrophin deficiency in the mdx model leads to a complex pathomechanistic scenario of secondary protein changes, which are not limited to a single pathway.
the dystrophin deficiency in the mdx4cv mouse model is associated with the loss of a large number of membrane proteins, including the dystrophin associated glycoproteins.
the organelle proteomics approach is well suited for the simultaneous pathoproteomic profiling of the dystrophin associated glycoproteome and secondary changes in skeletal muscle dystrophinopathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organelle focused comparative pathoproteomics of dystrophic skeletal muscle is a valuable tool to study the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex and its interaction partners.

the proteome of the microsomes of normal and dystrophic hind limb skeletal muscle can be successfully compared by a label free proteomic workflow, which is capable of identifying the most drastic changes of the dystrophin associated protein complex and secondary pathoproteomic effects in the mdx model of muscular dystrophy.

the organelle proteomics of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex in normal and dystrophin-deficient muscle is feasible and provides an unbiased approach for the discovery and validation of novel pathoproteomic biomarkers in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dystrophin associated protein complex is drastically reduced in the mdx mouse model of dystrophic muscle, whereas secondary pathoproteomic changes include the induction of metabolic pathways and an upregulation of the sarcolemma Na+/K+ATPase.

the organelle proteomics of dystrophic muscle tissue can be used to identify the full length dystrobrevin isoform Dystrobrevin 1 and the full length dystroglycan isoform Dystroglycan 2 as additional components of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex.

a comprehensive organelle proteomics analysis of the membrane fraction from skeletal muscle can be a useful tool to identify primary and secondary pathoproteomic changes in dystrophinopathies and other muscle diseases.
